name: M.C. Mehta v Union of India (Vehicular Pollution)
description: Public Interest Litigation (Writ Petition Civil no. 13029/1985) brought by the lawyer M.C. Mehta under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution for the protection of the fundamental right to a healthy environment (Art. 21 of the Constitution) in the face of the extremely high air pollution in Delhi and other metropolises, due largely to vehicular traffic and fuels.
outcome: The Supreme Court has issued dozens of orders over four decades, imposing: the introduction of unleaded petrol and catalytic converters, the conversion of Delhi’s public transport to CNG (2001, the first city in the world), the adoption of the Bharat standards, the closure of polluting industries, a ban on firecrackers (2018) and anti-smog plans. Recognition of the constitutional right to clean air; a global leading case on the “right to clean air”.
